1→# Feature Research
     2→
     3→**Domain:** Cloud Armor WAF Implementation on GCP Infrastructure
     4→**Researched:** 2026-02-24
     5→**Confidence:** HIGH (official GCP documentation) / MEDIUM (exclusion patterns per service type)
     6→
     7→---
     8→
     9→## Feature Landscape
    10→
    11→### Table Stakes (Users Expect These)
    12→
    13→Features that any serious WAF activation requires. Missing these means traffic gets blocked or the WAF is ineffective.
    14→
    15→| Feature | Why Expected | Complexity | Notes |
    16→|---------|--------------|------------|-------|
    17→| Attach policy to all LBs in scope | WAF does nothing until attached | LOW | `cloud_armor_policy` param already exists; needs `self_link` from sec project |
    18→| All rules stay in preview mode during rollout | Zero-downtime requirement; no production impact | LOW | Already the case; must not flip to enforce until analysis done |
    19→| Verbose logging enabled during analysis | Without it you cannot see which rule/field triggered; essential for false positive identification | LOW | `log_level = VERBOSE` on security policy; captures matchedFieldType, matchedFieldValue, matchedOffset |
    20→| Cloud Logging query for preview denies | Identify what WOULD have been blocked; basis for all exclusion decisions | LOW | Filter: `jsonPayload.previewSecurityPolicy.outcome="DENY"` in Cloud Logging |
    21→| Sensitivity level explicitly set per rule | Default evaluates ALL signatures; level 1 has lowest false positive risk | MEDIUM | Use `evaluatePreconfiguredWaf('sqli-v33-stable', {'sensitivity': 1})` syntax instead of bare `evaluatePreconfiguredExpr()` |
    22→| Centralize policy in sec project | Single policy to manage; consistent rules across all envs; only one policy to tune | MEDIUM | Cloud Armor policies are global within a project; attach via `self_link` from other projects — needs cross-project IAM |
    23→| Per-rule exclusions for high-risk services | Keycloak, Superset, Metabase, Django admin, file upload services WILL generate false positives at sensitivity 1 | HIGH | Uses `preconfigured_waf_config { exclusion { } }` block in Terraform |
    24→| Preview-to-enforce promotion checklist | Rules only protect when enforced; need defined criteria for when to switch | LOW | Define: zero false positives in 7-day preview window per rule |
    25→
    26→### Differentiators (Competitive Advantage)
    27→
    28→Features beyond baseline that improve security posture or operational efficiency.
    29→
    30→| Feature | Value Proposition | Complexity | Notes |
    31→|---------|-------------------|------------|-------|
    32→| Per-service sensitivity tuning | Different services have different risk profiles; generic sensitivity blocks legitimate traffic | MEDIUM | Airflow/Superset: sensitivity 1 only; Keycloak/Kong: sensitivity 1 with cookie/header exclusions; TMS API: sensitivity 2 acceptable |
    33→| Endpoint-scoped exclusions (URI-based) | Limit exclusions to specific paths, not entire services; tightest possible exception surface | MEDIUM | `request_uri { operator = "STARTS_WITH" value = "/auth/realms/" }` scopes exclusion to Keycloak auth endpoints only |
    34→| Rate limit differentiation per service tier | Auth endpoints need tighter rate limits than static content CDN; single 1000/min is blunt | MEDIUM | Rule priority ordering: stricter limits at lower priority numbers, evaluated first |
    35→| Custom log-based metric for preview deny rate | Alerts when a rule would block >X% of traffic in preview; early signal before enforcement | MEDIUM | Cloud Monitoring custom metric from Cloud Logging; threshold alert |
    36→| Google Stackdriver Monitoring uptime fix | Rule 1020 currently DENIES monitoring agent (bug in waf.tf — description says "allow" but action is deny) | LOW | Fix action or remove rule; monitoring agent must be whitelisted |
    37→
    38→### Anti-Features (Commonly Requested, Often Problematic)
    39→
    40→| Feature | Why Requested | Why Problematic | Alternative |
    41→|---------|---------------|-----------------|-------------|
    42→| Enforce all rules immediately after attach | "Let's just turn it on, we can fix false positives later" | Will block Keycloak logins, Superset SQL queries, file uploads — requires emergency rollback under pressure | Preview mode for minimum 7 days per rule; use logs to identify false positives before enforcing |
    43→| Single global sensitivity level across all services | Simpler to configure | Superset/Metabase send legitimate SQL; sensitivity 2+ on sqli will block them. Authentication services use tokens that trigger XSS/sessionfixation. One size fits none | Per-service exclusions scoped by URI or host header |
    44→| WAF at Cloud Run level (apps/cloudrun module) | Cloud Run services are behind LBs; seems logical | Cloud Run services in `apps/cloudrun` use domain mappings, not NEG backends with LBs that accept security policies. WAF applies at the LB backend service level | Apply WAF at the GKE/VM LBs that actually proxy to the backends |
    45→| Block-list all non-whitelisted user agents | Aggressive bot blocking | Legitimate monitoring tools, health checkers, partner integrations use generic agents | Keep existing user-agent rule in preview; only enforce after confirming no legitimate agents blocked |
    46→| Upgrade to newer OWASP CRS version during this milestone | v33-canary has newer signatures | Mixing version upgrade with initial activation makes it impossible to isolate false positive causes | Keep v33-stable for this milestone; upgrade in a dedicated subsequent milestone |
    47→| Full request body inspection for file uploads | Maximum security | Multipart/form-data binary content triggers LFI/RFI rules; performance penalty on large uploads | Exclude upload endpoints from body-inspection rules; scan at application layer instead |
    48→
    49→---
    50→
    51→## Feature Dependencies
    52→
    53→```
    54→[Centralize WAF in sec project]
    55→    └──requires──> [cross-project IAM: sec project Cloud Armor Admin bound to qa/prod SAs]
    56→    └──requires──> [waf.tf produces self_link output]
    57→    └──requires──> [load-balancer modules accept self_link not just policy name]
    58→
    59→[Per-rule exclusions]
    60→    └──requires──> [Verbose logging enabled]
    61→                       └──requires──> [Policy attached (even in preview)]
    62→    └──requires──> [Endpoint analysis complete per service]
    63→
    64→[Preview-to-enforce promotion]
    65→    └──requires──> [Per-rule exclusions configured]
    66→    └──requires──> [7-day preview window with zero false positives confirmed via logs]
    67→
    68→[Rate limit differentiation]
    69→    └──enhances──> [Existing rate_based_ban rule 1170]
    70→    └──conflicts──> [Single global rate limit rule — cannot have both]
    71→
    72→[Sensitivity tuning]
    73→    └──conflicts──> [Bare evaluatePreconfiguredExpr() — must switch to evaluatePreconfiguredWaf() with sensitivity param]
    74→```
    75→
    76→### Dependency Notes
    77→
    78→- **Centralize WAF requires cross-project IAM:** Cloud Armor `google_compute_security_policy.self_link` from sec project must be referenceable in backend service `security_policy` field of qa/bi/sha projects. GCP allows this if the caller has `compute.securityPolicies.use` on the policy resource. This must be validated — official docs are ambiguous on whether Cloud Armor Std (non-Enterprise) supports this.
    79→- **Exclusions require verbose logging first:** You cannot write correct exclusions without knowing which `matchedFieldType` and `matchedFieldValue` triggered. The analysis phase must run with verbose logging on.
    80→- **Sensitivity tuning conflicts with current rule syntax:** The existing `waf.tf` uses `evaluatePreconfiguredExpr('sqli-v33-stable')` which does not accept a sensitivity parameter. Switching to `evaluatePreconfiguredWaf('sqli-v33-stable', {'sensitivity': 1})` is a required change to enable per-rule sensitivity control.
    81→- **Rule 1020 bug:** Current waf.tf has rule 1020 with `action = "deny(403)"` and description "Permitir GoogleStackdriverMonitoring-UptimeChecks" — description and action contradict each other. This blocks the monitoring agent if enforced. Must resolve before enforcement.
    82→
    83→---
    84→
    85→## MVP Definition
    86→
    87→### Launch With (v1 — QA Rollout)
    88→
    89→Minimum set to have WAF attached and generating analyzable data in QA without false positives.
    90→
    91→- [ ] Fix rule 1020 (monitoring agent — deny vs allow contradiction)
    92→- [ ] Switch all preconfigured rules from `evaluatePreconfiguredExpr()` to `evaluatePreconfiguredWaf()` with explicit `sensitivity: 1`
    93→- [ ] Enable verbose logging (`log_level = VERBOSE`) on WAF policy
    94→- [ ] Centralize policy in sec project and output `self_link`
    95→- [ ] Attach WAF policy (preview mode only) to `apps/gke` LB in qa workspace
    96→- [ ] Attach WAF policy (preview mode only) to `apps/frontends` LB in qa workspace
    97→- [ ] Attach WAF policy (preview mode only) to `apps/apps` LB in qa workspace
    98→- [ ] Establish Cloud Logging query baseline for preview deny events
    99→- [ ] Document false positive findings per service from preview logs
   100→
   101→### Add After Validation (v1.x — Exclusions + Remaining LBs)
   102→
   103→After baseline analysis shows which services generate false positives and which rules trigger:
   104→
   105→- [ ] Add `preconfigured_waf_config` exclusions for Keycloak (session fixation cookie values, auth token headers)
   106→- [ ] Add `preconfigured_waf_config` exclusions for Superset/Metabase (sqli rule — SQL query params/POST body on `/api/` paths)
   107→- [ ] Add `preconfigured_waf_config` exclusions for support-administration Django admin (XSS exclusion for CSRF token cookie/header, POST body on `/admin/` paths)
   108→- [ ] Add `preconfigured_waf_config` exclusions for excel-loader/lms-excel-loader (LFI/RFI exclusion for multipart upload URI)
   109→- [ ] Add `preconfigured_waf_config` exclusions for Kong (method enforcement — Kong proxies non-standard methods)
   110→- [ ] Attach to remaining QA LBs: `apps/airflow`, `common/apps`, `bi/apps`, `bi/wrenai-poc`
   111→- [ ] Create Cloud Monitoring alert for preview deny rate spike (>5% of requests denied in preview)
   112→
   113→### Future Consideration (v2+ — Enforcement)
   114→
   115→After QA preview window shows clean logs for 7+ days:
   116→
   117→- [ ] Promote rules from preview to enforce, service by service, starting with lowest-risk (static frontends)
   118→- [ ] Differentiate rate limits per service tier (auth: 100/min, APIs: 1000/min, static: unlimited)
   119→- [ ] Rollout to staging workspace
   120→- [ ] Rollout to production workspace
   121→- [ ] Evaluate Adaptive Protection (volumetric DDoS ML detection) — separate billing consideration
   122→
   123→---
   124→
   125→## Feature Prioritization Matrix
   126→
   127→| Feature | User Value | Implementation Cost | Priority |
   128→|---------|------------|---------------------|----------|
   129→| Fix rule 1020 monitoring agent bug | HIGH — prevents monitor blackouts | LOW | P1 |
   130→| Switch to evaluatePreconfiguredWaf() with sensitivity | HIGH — reduces false positives before any attach | LOW | P1 |
   131→| Enable verbose logging | HIGH — required for any false positive analysis | LOW | P1 |
   132→| Attach to GKE LB in preview mode | HIGH — WAF is useless without attachment | LOW | P1 |
   133→| Centralize policy in sec project | MEDIUM — operational simplicity | MEDIUM | P1 |
   134→| Keycloak exclusions | HIGH — auth flow blocks = total outage | MEDIUM | P1 |
   135→| Superset/Metabase exclusions | HIGH — SQL query builders will always trigger sqli | MEDIUM | P1 |
   136→| Django admin (support-administration) exclusions | MEDIUM — internal admin, lower blast radius | MEDIUM | P2 |
   137→| File upload service exclusions | MEDIUM — specific endpoints, not all traffic | MEDIUM | P2 |
   138→| Kong exclusions | MEDIUM — gateway proxies everything | MEDIUM | P2 |
   139→| Cloud Monitoring alert for preview deny rate | MEDIUM — operational visibility | LOW | P2 |
   140→| Rate limit differentiation per service | MEDIUM — improved protection vs current blanket 1000/min | HIGH | P3 |
   141→| Adaptive Protection | LOW — separate billing tier, out of scope | HIGH | P3 |
   142→
   143→**Priority key:**
   144→- P1: Must have for QA rollout milestone
   145→- P2: Should have before marking milestone complete
   146→- P3: Future milestone consideration
   147→
   148→---
   149→
   150→## Service-Specific Exclusion Patterns
   151→
   152→This section maps each high-risk service to the specific Cloud Armor exclusion configuration needed.
   153→
   154→### Keycloak (auth-domain service)
   155→
   156→**Triggers:** `sessionfixation-v33-stable`, `xss-v33-stable`
   157→**Why:** Keycloak uses complex JWT tokens in cookies/headers and session management patterns that resemble session fixation attacks. OAuth2 redirect URLs contain parameters that trigger XSS rules.
   158→
   159→**Exclusion pattern:**
   160→```hcl
   161→# On the sessionfixation rule
   162→exclusion {
   163→  target_rule_set = "sessionfixation-v33-stable"
   164→  request_cookie {
   165→    operator = "STARTS_WITH"
   166→    value    = "AUTH_SESSION_ID"
   167→  }
   168→  request_cookie {
   169→    operator = "STARTS_WITH"
   170→    value    = "KEYCLOAK_SESSION"
   171→  }
   172→  request_header {
   173→    operator = "EQUALS"
   174→    value    = "authorization"  # Bearer token inspection
   175→  }
   176→}
   177→# Scope to Keycloak host only via separate rule priority or CEL host match
   178→```
   179→
   180→**Confidence:** MEDIUM — pattern based on OWASP CRS session fixation rule behavior; validate against verbose logs.
   181→
   182→### Kong API Gateway (kong service)
   183→
   184→**Triggers:** `methodenforcement-v33-stable`, `protocolattack-v33-stable`
   185→**Why:** Kong proxies requests using non-standard HTTP methods (PATCH, OPTIONS with bodies, CONNECT). Protocol attack rules flag some Kong-specific header patterns used in upstream communication.
   186→
   187→**Exclusion pattern:**
   188→```hcl
   189→exclusion {
   190→  target_rule_set = "methodenforcement-v33-stable"
   191→  request_uri {
   192→    operator = "STARTS_WITH"
   193→    value    = "/"   # Full bypass — Kong validates methods internally
   194→  }
   195→}
   196→```
   197→
   198→**Note:** If Kong enforces its own method validation, full URI bypass on methodenforcement is acceptable. Validate by checking Kong's allowed methods config.
   199→**Confidence:** MEDIUM — methodology enforcement exclusion is standard for API gateway proxies.
   200→
   201→### Superset and Metabase (bi/apps LB)
   202→
   203→**Triggers:** `sqli-v33-stable`, `json-sqli-canary`
   204→**Why:** Both are SQL query builder tools. Users legitimately type SQL into query interfaces. POST body and query parameters WILL contain SQL syntax that triggers sqli rules at any sensitivity level. There is no sensitivity low enough to avoid this.
   205→
   206→**Exclusion pattern:**
   207→```hcl
   208→# sqli rule — exclude POST body params on API paths
   209→exclusion {
   210→  target_rule_set = "sqli-v33-stable"
   211→  request_uri {
   212→    operator = "STARTS_WITH"
   213→    value    = "/api/"
   214→  }
   215→  request_query_param {
   216→    operator = "EQUALS_ANY"   # all query params on API paths
   217→  }
   218→}
   219→# json-sqli — same, exclude API body
   220→exclusion {
   221→  target_rule_set = "json-sqli-canary"
   222→  request_uri {
   223→    operator = "STARTS_WITH"
   224→    value    = "/api/"
   225→  }
   226→}
   227→```
   228→
   229→**Alternative:** Scope WAF to NOT attach to bi/apps LB at all in v1 — BI tools are internal, accessible only via VPN or Cloudflare Access. WAF adds marginal value vs. false positive risk here.
   230→**Confidence:** HIGH — any SQL query builder will trigger sqli rules; this is a known pattern.
   231→
   232→### support-administration (Django Admin)
   233→
   234→**Triggers:** `xss-v33-stable`, `sqli-v33-stable`
   235→**Why:** Django admin sends CSRF tokens in POST bodies and cookies. CSRF token values are long random strings that can resemble XSS payloads. Admin forms can contain user-generated content (addresses, names with special characters) that triggers XSS.
   236→
   237→**Exclusion pattern:**
   238→```hcl
   239→exclusion {
   240→  target_rule_set = "xss-v33-stable"
   241→  request_cookie {
   242→    operator = "EQUALS"
   243→    value    = "csrftoken"   # Django CSRF cookie value excluded from XSS inspection
   244→  }
   245→  request_header {
   246→    operator = "EQUALS"
   247→    value    = "x-csrftoken"  # CSRF token header value excluded
   248→  }
   249→  request_uri {
   250→    operator = "STARTS_WITH"
   251→    value    = "/admin/"
   252→  }
   253→}
   254→```
   255→
   256→**Confidence:** HIGH — Django CSRF token exclusion is a documented WAF false positive pattern across all WAF vendors.
   257→
   258→### excel-loader and lms-excel-loader (file upload services)
   259→
   260→**Triggers:** `lfi-v33-stable`, `rfi-v33-stable`
   261→**Why:** Multipart file upload POST bodies contain binary data and filename paths. LFI rules pattern-match path traversal sequences (`../`) and Windows paths, which can appear in Excel file metadata and column names.
   262→
   263→**Exclusion pattern:**
   264→```hcl
   265→exclusion {
   266→  target_rule_set = "lfi-v33-stable"
   267→  request_uri {
   268→    operator = "STARTS_WITH"
   269→    value    = "/main/upload"   # excel-loader upload endpoint
   270→  }
   271→}
   272→exclusion {
   273→  target_rule_set = "rfi-v33-stable"
   274→  request_uri {
   275→    operator = "STARTS_WITH"
   276→    value    = "/main/upload"
   277→  }
   278→}
   279→```
   280→
   281→**Note:** Exact upload path for lms-excel-loader must be confirmed from application routing. Do not exclude the entire service — only the upload endpoint.
   282→**Confidence:** MEDIUM — LFI/multipart false positives are a documented pattern; exact path requires validation.
   283→
   284→### backoffice-api (admin operations)
   285→
   286→**Triggers:** `sqli-v33-stable` at sensitivity 2+
   287→**Why:** Backoffice API is described in PROJECT.md as performing "admin operations, possible SQL-like input." At sensitivity 1 (recommended baseline) this should be low risk. Validate via logs before adding exclusions.
   288→
   289→**Exclusion pattern:** None needed at sensitivity 1. Monitor preview logs first.
   290→**Confidence:** MEDIUM — defer until logs confirm actual trigger.
   291→
   292→---
   293→
   294→## Monitoring and Logging Features
   295→
   296→### Essential for Production WAF Operation
   297→
   298→| Feature | What It Provides | How to Configure | Confidence |
   299→|---------|-----------------|------------------|------------|
   300→| Verbose logging | Shows `matchedFieldType`, `matchedFieldValue`, `matchedOffset` — identifies exact field triggering each WAF rule | `log_level = VERBOSE` on `google_compute_security_policy` | HIGH |
   301→| Preview deny log query | Shows all requests that WOULD have been blocked; basis for false positive analysis | Cloud Logging filter: `jsonPayload.previewSecurityPolicy.outcome="DENY"` | HIGH |
   302→| `preconfiguredExprIds` in logs | Shows which specific rule ID triggered (e.g., `owasp-crs-v030301-id942200-sqli`); required for writing targeted exclusions | Included automatically in Cloud Armor logs; no config needed | HIGH |
   303→| Cloud Monitoring WAF dashboard | Out-of-box "Cloud Armor policies overview" dashboard; shows allowed/denied/preview-denied breakdowns per backend | Available in Cloud Console → Monitoring → Dashboards | HIGH |
   304→| Enforce deny alert | Alert when enforced deny rate exceeds threshold; indicates either attack or misconfiguration | Custom log-based metric: `jsonPayload.enforcedSecurityPolicy.outcome="DENY"` count > threshold | MEDIUM |
   305→| Preview deny rate alert | Alert when preview would block >5% of legitimate traffic; catch false positives before enforcement | Custom log-based metric on `previewSecurityPolicy.outcome="DENY"` | MEDIUM |
   306→
   307→### Logging Fields Available (Cloud Armor in LB Logs)
   308→
   309→From verbose logging (`matchedField*` fields), the following are actionable for tuning:
   310→- `matchedFieldType` — which part of request triggered (BODY, HEADER_VALUES, ARG_VALUES, URI, COOKIE_VALUES, USER_AGENT)
   311→- `matchedFieldName` — the header/cookie/param name that triggered
   312→- `matchedFieldValue` — up to 16 bytes of the matching content
   313→- `preconfiguredExprIds` — specific OWASP rule ID (maps to exact WAF signature for targeted exclusion)
   314→- `previewSecurityPolicy.name` / `.priority` — which rule would have applied
   315→- `enforcedSecurityPolicy.outcome` — ALLOW or DENY in enforce mode
   316→
   317→### What Cloud Logging Cannot Do
   318→
   319→- Does not log full request body (only 16-byte snippets in verbose mode)
   320→- Does not log all HTTP headers by default (only User-Agent reliably)
   321→- Verbose logging has PII risk — disable after tuning phase, not for permanent production use
   322→- Log-based metrics add cost at high traffic volumes; sample if needed after analysis phase
   323→
   324→---
   325→
   326→## Cross-Project WAF Policy Architecture
   327→
   328→### Critical Constraint (Confidence: LOW — needs validation)
   329→
   330→Cloud Armor policy `self_link` can be referenced from backend services in other projects. The `security_policy` field on `google_compute_backend_service` accepts a full resource URL. However:
   331→
   332→1. Official docs focus on same-project attachment
   333→2. Cloud Armor Enterprise mentions cross-project as an explicit feature tied to billing enrollment
   334→3. It is **unclear from available documentation** whether Cloud Armor Standard (non-Enterprise) supports cross-project backend service attachment via `self_link`
   335→
   336→**Risk:** The centralization architecture (single policy in sec project, attached from qa/bi/sha projects) may require Cloud Armor Enterprise or may not be supported at all in Standard tier.
   337→
   338→**Mitigation options:**
   339→1. Validate with a test Terraform apply before committing to this architecture
   340→2. Fallback: Keep per-workspace policies (current architecture) but sync them via shared module — more management overhead but definitely supported
   341→3. Use `google_compute_security_policy` data source from the sec project to fetch the policy and reference its `self_link` — test if this works cross-project
   342→
   343→This is the highest-risk architectural assumption in the milestone. Validate in Phase 1 before designing the centralization approach.
   344→
   345→---
   346→
   347→## Sources
   348→
   349→- [Google Cloud Armor WAF Rule Tuning](https://cloud.google.com/armor/docs/rule-tuning) — Exclusion patterns, field types, operators, sensitivity levels (HIGH confidence)
   350→- [Cloud Armor Preconfigured WAF Rules Overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/waf-rules) — Rule categories, sensitivity levels, false positive risk by rule (HIGH confidence)
   351→- [Cloud Armor Best Practices](https://cloud.google.com/armor/docs/best-practices) — Preview mode strategy, sensitivity starting point, verbose logging recommendation (HIGH confidence)
   352→- [Cloud Armor Verbose Logging](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/verbose-logging) — Available log fields, Terraform config gap, privacy considerations (HIGH confidence)
   353→- [Cloud Armor Monitoring](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/monitoring) — Available metrics, dashboard, alerting (HIGH confidence)
   354→- [Cloud Armor Request Logging](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/request-logging) — Log fields, preview vs enforce log distinction (HIGH confidence)
   355→- [Terraform google_compute_security_policy](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google/blob/main/website/docs/r/compute_security_policy.html.markdown) — `preconfigured_waf_config` schema, exclusion operators (HIGH confidence)
   356→- [Cloud Armor Rate Limiting](https://cloud.google.com/armor/docs/rate-limiting-overview) — Per-endpoint thresholds, per-IP enforcement, regional behavior (HIGH confidence)
   357→- [Cloud Armor Security Policy Overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/security-policy-overview) — Cross-project attachment limitations (LOW confidence — docs are ambiguous)
   358→- [Cloud Armor Example Policies](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/example-policies) — Supplementary configuration examples (MEDIUM confidence)
   359→
   360→---
   361→
   362→*Feature research for: Cloud Armor WAF Implementation — Liftit GCP Infrastructure*
   363→*Researched: 2026-02-24*

1→# Architecture Research
     2→
     3→**Domain:** Cross-project Cloud Armor WAF centralization for multi-project GCP infrastructure
     4→**Researched:** 2026-02-24
     5→**Confidence:** HIGH (GCP behavior verified via official docs; Terraform patterns verified via provider docs and community)
     6→
     7→## Critical Finding: Cross-Project Policy Sharing Is Not Possible
     8→
     9→Cloud Armor `google_compute_security_policy` is a project-scoped global resource. A security policy created in `security-454414` (sec workspace) **cannot be directly attached** to a backend service in `qa-apps-454414`, `prod-apps-454414`, `liftit-bi`, or `shared-016`. The `cloud_armor_policy` parameter of `google_compute_backend_service` only accepts policies owned by the same project as the backend service.
    10→
    11→This means the originally stated goal — "single centralized policy in sec project, referenced cross-project by all LBs" — is architecturally invalid and will fail at the GCP API level.
    12→
    13→**Source:** GCP Cloud Armor documentation (per-project quotas, policy-to-backend-service attachment scoped to same project). Verified via [Configure Cloud Armor security policies](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/configure-security-policies) and [Quotas and limits](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/quotas). Confidence: HIGH.
    14→
    15→The viable centralized strategy is: **one Terraform module (sec/waf) deploys identical policies into every target project using multi-project providers**, with the WAF policy self_link output used by each LB module via remote state.
    16→
    17→---
    18→
    19→## System Overview
    20→
    21→```
    22→┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    23→│                         sec/waf Module                              │
    24→│         (Terraform workspace: sec, run once, manages all)           │
    25→├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    26→│  provider "google" { alias = "qa"   project = "qa-apps-454414"  }  │
    27→│  provider "google" { alias = "prod" project = "prod-apps-454414"}  │
    28→│  provider "google" { alias = "sha"  project = "shared-016"      }  │
    29→│  provider "google" { alias = "bi"   project = "liftit-bi"       }  │
    30→│  provider "google" { alias = "sec"  project = "security-454414" }  │
    31→├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    32→│  module "waf_qa"   { source = tf-modules//waf  provider = qa   }   │
    33→│  module "waf_prod" { source = tf-modules//waf  provider = prod }   │
    34→│  module "waf_sha"  { source = tf-modules//waf  provider = sha  }   │
    35→│  module "waf_bi"   { source = tf-modules//waf  provider = bi   }   │
    36→└────────┬────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────-─┘
    37→         │ outputs:           │ outputs:
    38→         │ qa_policy_self_link│ prod_policy_self_link...
    39→         ▼                    ▼
    40→┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    41→│                    Terraform Remote State                           │
    42→│              bucket: liftit-tf-state / prefix: sec/waf             │
    43→│           workspace: sec (single state for all deployments)        │
    44→└────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    45→         │ data "terraform_remote_state" "waf" { workspace = "sec" }
    46→         │
    47→  ┌──────┴──────────────────────────────────┐
    48→  │                                         │
    49→  ▼                                         ▼
    50→┌─────────────────────┐         ┌───────────────────────┐
    51→│  apps/gke (qa ws)   │         │  apps/gke (prod ws)   │
    52→│  apps/frontends     │         │  apps/frontends       │
    53→│  apps/airflow       │         │  apps/airflow         │
    54→│  apps/apps          │         │  apps/apps            │
    55→│                     │         │                       │
    56→│  cloud_armor_policy │         │  cloud_armor_policy   │
    57→│  = remote_state     │         │  = remote_state       │
    58→│    .waf.outputs     │         │    .waf.outputs       │
    59→│    .qa_policy_link  │         │    .prod_policy_link  │
    60→└─────────────────────┘         └───────────────────────┘
    61→
    62→┌─────────────────────┐         ┌───────────────────────┐
    63→│  common/apps (sha)  │         │  bi/apps (bi ws)      │
    64→│                     │         │  bi/wrenai-poc        │
    65→│  cloud_armor_policy │         │                       │
    66→│  = sha_policy_link  │         │  cloud_armor_policy   │
    67→└─────────────────────┘         │  = bi_policy_link     │
    68→                                └───────────────────────┘
    69→```
    70→
    71→## Component Responsibilities
    72→
    73→| Component | Responsibility | Current State | Target State |
    74→|-----------|----------------|---------------|--------------|
    75→| `sec/waf` | WAF policy definitions — rules, priorities, rate limits, IP whitelist | Deploys one policy per workspace (qa/staging/prod/sha/sec) | Deploys policies per target project from single run using multi-provider |
    76→| `tf-modules//waf` | Creates `google_compute_security_policy` + `google_compute_security_policy_rule` | Unchanged | Unchanged — module stays as-is |
    77→| `tf-modules//load-balancer` | Accepts `cloud_armor_policy` string (self_link or name) | `null` | Receives self_link from remote state |
    78→| `apps/gke`, `apps/frontends`, `apps/airflow`, `apps/apps`, `common/apps`, `bi/apps`, `bi/wrenai-poc` | Attach WAF policy to their LB backend services | `cloud_armor_policy = null` | `cloud_armor_policy = data.terraform_remote_state.waf.outputs.{env}_policy_self_link` |
    79→
    80→## Recommended Module Structure
    81→
    82→```
    83→sec/waf/
    84→├── backend.tf          # GCS state: liftit-tf-state / prefix sec/waf
    85→├── versions.tf         # Terraform ~> 1.14, Google ~> 7.0 (NO workspace strategy change needed)
    86→├── providers.tf        # NEW: multi-alias providers for qa/prod/sha/bi/sec projects
    87→├── locals.tf           # IP whitelist per env, rule definitions
    88→├── remote-state.tf     # folders, dns (unchanged)
    89→├── waf.tf              # CHANGED: one waf module call per target project, each with provider alias
    90→├── outputs.tf          # CHANGED: export self_link per project (qa_policy_self_link, etc.)
    91→└── CLAUDE.md
    92→
    93→# Consumer modules add to remote-state.tf:
    94→data "terraform_remote_state" "waf" {
    95→  backend   = "gcs"
    96→  workspace = "sec"
    97→  config = {
    98→    bucket = "liftit-tf-state"
    99→    prefix = "sec/waf"
   100→  }
   101→}
   102→```
   103→
   104→## Architectural Patterns
   105→
   106→### Pattern 1: Multi-Provider in sec/waf (NEW)
   107→
   108→**What:** Deploy identical WAF policies across multiple GCP projects from a single Terraform state using provider aliases.
   109→
   110→**When to use:** When a resource cannot be shared cross-project (like Cloud Armor policies) but must maintain identical configuration. Eliminates per-workspace deploys.
   111→
   112→**Trade-offs:** Single state file manages all WAF policies — simpler rule management, but a bug in `waf.tf` affects all projects simultaneously. Requires Terraform SA in sec to have `compute.securityPolicies.*` in every target project.
   113→
   114→**Example:**
   115→
   116→```hcl
   117→# sec/waf/providers.tf
   118→provider "google" {
   119→  alias   = "qa"
   120→  project = "qa-apps-454414"
   121→}
   122→
   123→provider "google" {
   124→  alias   = "prod"
   125→  project = "prod-apps-454414"
   126→}
   127→
   128→provider "google" {
   129→  alias   = "sha"
   130→  project = "shared-016"
   131→}
   132→
   133→provider "google" {
   134→  alias   = "bi"
   135→  project = "liftit-bi"
   136→}
   137→
   138→# sec/waf/waf.tf
   139→module "waf_qa" {
   140→  source             = "git::ssh://git@github.com/liftitapp/tf-modules.git//waf"
   141→  providers          = { google = google.qa }
   142→  policy_name        = "liftit-waf-qa"
   143→  policy_description = "Politica de seguridad WAF Liftit - QA"
   144→  rules              = local.waf_rules_qa  # shared base + qa-specific exclusions
   145→}
   146→
   147→module "waf_prod" {
   148→  source             = "git::ssh://git@github.com/liftitapp/tf-modules.git//waf"
   149→  providers          = { google = google.prod }
   150→  policy_name        = "liftit-waf-prod"
   151→  policy_description = "Politica de seguridad WAF Liftit - Prod"
   152→  rules              = local.waf_rules_prod  # same base rules, potentially different exclusions
   153→}
   154→
   155→module "waf_sha" {
   156→  source             = "git::ssh://git@github.com/liftitapp/tf-modules.git//waf"
   157→  providers          = { google = google.sha }
   158→  policy_name        = "liftit-waf-sha"
   159→  policy_description = "Politica de seguridad WAF Liftit - SHA"
   160→  rules              = local.waf_rules_base
   161→}
   162→
   163→module "waf_bi" {
   164→  source             = "git::ssh://git@github.com/liftitapp/tf-modules.git//waf"
   165→  providers          = { google = google.bi }
   166→  policy_name        = "liftit-waf-bi"
   167→  policy_description = "Politica de seguridad WAF Liftit - BI"
   168→  rules              = local.waf_rules_bi  # exclude superset/metabase SQLi paths
   169→}
   170→```
   171→
   172→### Pattern 2: Remote State Output Propagation (EXISTING, EXTENDED)
   173→
   174→**What:** Consumer modules read WAF policy self_links from `sec/waf` remote state and pass them to the load balancer module.
   175→
   176→**When to use:** This is the existing Liftit remote state pattern — already used for KMS keys, VPC IDs, SSL certs. Extending it to WAF policy outputs is consistent with the codebase.
   177→
   178→**Trade-offs:** Creates a hard dependency — LB modules cannot apply until `sec/waf` has been applied first. This is acceptable because `sec/waf` is a Layer 2 resource and LBs are Layer 5.
   179→
   180→**Example:**
   181→
   182→```hcl
   183→# In apps/gke/remote-state.tf (ADD)
   184→data "terraform_remote_state" "waf" {
   185→  backend   = "gcs"
   186→  workspace = "sec"
   187→  config = {
   188→    bucket = "liftit-tf-state"
   189→    prefix = "sec/waf"
   190→  }
   191→}
   192→
   193→# In apps/gke/load-balancer.tf (CHANGE)
   194→module "gke-apps-load-balancer" {
   195→  source             = "git::ssh://git@github.com/liftitapp/tf-modules.git//load-balancer"
   196→  # ... existing params ...
   197→  cloud_armor_policy = data.terraform_remote_state.waf.outputs.qa_policy_self_link
   198→  # For prod workspace: .outputs.prod_policy_self_link
   199→}
   200→```
   201→
   202→```hcl
   203→# sec/waf/outputs.tf (REPLACE current outputs)
   204→output "qa_policy_self_link" {
   205→  value = module.waf_qa.policy_self_link
   206→}
   207→
   208→output "prod_policy_self_link" {
   209→  value = module.waf_prod.policy_self_link
   210→}
   211→
   212→output "sha_policy_self_link" {
   213→  value = module.waf_sha.policy_self_link
   214→}
   215→
   216→output "bi_policy_self_link" {
   217→  value = module.waf_bi.policy_self_link
   218→}
   219→```
   220→
   221→### Pattern 3: Per-Environment WAF Rule Exclusions via Locals (NEW)
   222→
   223→**What:** Store WAF rule sets as Terraform locals in `sec/waf/locals.tf`. A base rule set is shared across all environments. High-risk services get additional `preconfigured_waf_config` exclusions added to the rule map for their environment's policy.
   224→
   225→**When to use:** When the same Cloud Armor WAF policy must protect different services with different false-positive profiles. Superset/Metabase (BI project) trigger SQLi rules; Keycloak triggers session fixation rules; Django admin triggers method enforcement.
   226→
   227→**Trade-offs:** Exclusions live in `sec/waf`, not in the service's own module. A developer adding a new microservice cannot self-service add WAF exclusions — they must modify `sec/waf`. This is intentional: WAF exclusions are a security decision, not a per-service concern.
   228→
   229→**Example:**
   230→
   231→```hcl
   232→# sec/waf/locals.tf — rule set composition
   233→locals {
   234→  # Base rules — identical across all environments
   235→  waf_rules_base = {
   236→    "1000" = { ... ip whitelist ... }
   237→    "1010" = { ... user-agent blocking ... }
   238→    "1030" = { action = "deny(403)", preview = true, expr = "evaluatePreconfiguredExpr('sqli-v33-stable')" }
   239→    # ... other OWASP rules ...
   240→    "1170" = { ... rate limiting ... }
   241→  }
   242→
   243→  # BI-specific: superset and metabase are SQL query builders.
   244→  # SQLi rules will false-positive on valid SQL queries submitted by authenticated users.
   245→  # Exclude SQLi inspection for known BI tool hosts.
   246→  waf_rules_bi = merge(local.waf_rules_base, {
   247→    "1030" = {
   248→      action         = "deny(403)"
   249→      description    = "SQLi - con exclusion para superset/metabase"
   250→      preview        = true
   251→      expr           = "evaluatePreconfiguredExpr('sqli-v33-stable') && !request.headers['host'].matches('(?i:superset|metabase)')"
   252→    }
   253→  })
   254→
   255→  # QA-specific: may need different IP whitelist
   256→  waf_rules_qa = merge(local.waf_rules_base, {
   257→    "1000" = {
   258→      action         = "allow"
   259→      description    = "IPs de confianza - QA"
   260→      preview        = false
   261→      versioned_expr = "SRC_IPS_V1"
   262→      src_ip_ranges  = ["34.23.50.140"]  # QA NAT IP
   263→    }
   264→  })
   265→
   266→  waf_rules_prod = merge(local.waf_rules_base, {
   267→    "1000" = {
   268→      action         = "allow"
   269→      description    = "IPs de confianza - Prod"
   270→      preview        = false
   271→      versioned_expr = "SRC_IPS_V1"
   272→      src_ip_ranges  = ["34.74.192.228"]  # Prod NAT IP
   273→    }
   274→  })
   275→}
   276→```
   277→
   278→### Pattern 4: Workspace-Conditional Policy Reference in Consumer Modules
   279→
   280→**What:** Consumer modules that run across multiple workspaces (qa/staging/prod) select the correct WAF policy self_link from remote state based on `terraform.workspace`.
   281→
   282→**When to use:** `apps/gke`, `apps/frontends`, `apps/airflow`, `apps/apps` are all multi-workspace. They must reference the right policy for their project.
   283→
   284→**Trade-offs:** Adds a conditional expression to the `cloud_armor_policy` parameter. Simple and consistent with existing workspace-based logic already present in these modules (e.g., `neg_ids[terraform.workspace]` pattern).
   285→
   286→**Example:**
   287→
   288→```hcl
   289→# apps/gke/load-balancer.tf
   290→locals {
   291→  waf_policy_map = {
   292→    qa      = data.terraform_remote_state.waf.outputs.qa_policy_self_link
   293→    staging = data.terraform_remote_state.waf.outputs.staging_policy_self_link
   294→    prod    = data.terraform_remote_state.waf.outputs.prod_policy_self_link
   295→  }
   296→}
   297→
   298→module "gke-apps-load-balancer" {
   299→  # ...
   300→  cloud_armor_policy = local.waf_policy_map[terraform.workspace]
   301→}
   302→```
   303→
   304→For single-workspace modules (`common/apps` runs in `sha`, `bi/apps` runs in `bi`), use the specific output directly:
   305→
   306→```hcl
   307→# common/apps/load-balancer.tf
   308→cloud_armor_policy = data.terraform_remote_state.waf.outputs.sha_policy_self_link
   309→
   310→# bi/apps/load-balancer.tf
   311→cloud_armor_policy = data.terraform_remote_state.waf.outputs.bi_policy_self_link
   312→```
   313→
   314→## Data Flow
   315→
   316→### WAF Policy Deployment Flow
   317→
   318→```
   319→1. Engineer modifies sec/waf/waf.tf or locals.tf
   320→        ↓
   321→2. terraform apply (workspace: sec)
   322→   → deploys google_compute_security_policy to qa-apps-454414
   323→   → deploys google_compute_security_policy to prod-apps-454414
   324→   → deploys google_compute_security_policy to shared-016
   325→   → deploys google_compute_security_policy to liftit-bi
   326→   → writes outputs to GCS: liftit-tf-state/sec/waf/sec.tfstate
   327→        ↓
   328→3. Consumer module runs (e.g., apps/gke, workspace: qa)
   329→   → reads data.terraform_remote_state.waf (workspace=sec)
   330→   → gets outputs.qa_policy_self_link
   331→   → passes to module.gke-apps-load-balancer cloud_armor_policy param
   332→   → tf-modules//load-balancer sets security_policy on google_compute_backend_service
   333→        ↓
   334→4. GCP attaches the Cloud Armor policy to the backend service
   335→   → Traffic through the LB is inspected (preview mode: logged but not blocked)
   336→```
   337→
   338→### Rule Exclusion Addition Flow
   339→
   340→```
   341→1. Endpoint analysis identifies false positive (e.g., Superset SQL editor)
   342→        ↓
   343→2. Add exclusion to sec/waf/locals.tf (waf_rules_bi or new expr in rule)
   344→        ↓
   345→3. terraform apply (workspace: sec)
   346→   → updates google_compute_security_policy_rule in liftit-bi project
   347→        ↓
   348→4. bi/apps LB module already references bi_policy_self_link — no change needed
   349→   (Policy is updated in-place; no re-apply of consumer modules required)
   350→```
   351→
   352→### IP Whitelist Update Flow
   353→
   354→```
   355→sec/waf/waf.tf local.ip_whitelist[workspace]
   356→        ↓ (currently per-workspace)
   357→Target: move to per-project keys in locals.tf
   358→local.ip_whitelist = {
   359→  qa      = ["34.23.50.140"]       # qa-apps-454414 NAT
   360→  staging = ["35.196.126.133"]     # stg-apps-454414 NAT
   361→  prod    = ["34.74.192.228"]      # prod-apps-454414 NAT
   362→  sha     = ["35.185.50.62"]       # shared-016 NAT
   363→  bi      = [...]                  # liftit-bi NAT (add when known)
   364→  sec     = ["35.227.65.152"]      # security-454414 NAT
   365→}
   366→```
   367→
   368→## New vs Modified Components
   369→
   370→### NEW
   371→
   372→| Component | What Changes | File |
   373→|-----------|--------------|------|
   374→| `sec/waf/providers.tf` | Add provider aliases for qa, prod, sha, bi | New file (or extend existing) |
   375→| `sec/waf/waf.tf` | Replace single module call with one per project | Rewrite |
   376→| `sec/waf/outputs.tf` | Export `{project}_policy_self_link` per project | Rewrite |
   377→| `sec/waf/locals.tf` | Add `waf_rules_{env}` locals for per-env exclusions | Extend |

   380→
   381→| Component | What Changes | File |
   382→|-----------|--------------|------|
   383→| `apps/gke/remote-state.tf` | Add `terraform_remote_state.waf` data source | Add block |
   384→| `apps/gke/load-balancer.tf` | Set `cloud_armor_policy = waf_policy_map[workspace]` | Change 1 line |

   386→| `apps/frontends/load-balancer.tf` | Set `cloud_armor_policy = waf_policy_map[workspace]` | Change 1 line |

   396→| `bi/wrenai-poc/load-balancer.tf` | Set `cloud_armor_policy = bi_policy_self_link` | Change 1 line |
   397→
   398→### UNCHANGED
   399→
   400→| Component | Reason |
   401→|-----------|--------|

   403→| `tf-modules//load-balancer` | Already accepts `cloud_armor_policy` string — no interface change needed |
   404→| `sec/waf/backend.tf` | State stays at `liftit-tf-state/sec/waf`, workspace `sec` |
   405→| `apps/gke/gke.tf` | GKE cluster unaffected |
   406→| `sec/waf/remote-state.tf` | Folder + DNS remote state unchanged |
   407→
   408→## Build Order
   409→
   410→The following sequence must be respected due to remote state dependencies:
   411→
   412→```
   413→Step 1: sec/waf  (workspace: sec)
   414→   → Deploys policies to qa-apps-454414, prod-apps-454414, shared-016, liftit-bi
   415→   → Writes self_links to GCS state
   416→   → MUST complete before any LB consumer module runs
   417→
   418→Step 2 (parallel, QA milestone only):
   419→   → apps/gke        (workspace: qa)   — reads qa_policy_self_link
   420→   → apps/frontends  (workspace: qa)   — reads qa_policy_self_link
   421→   → apps/airflow    (workspace: qa)   — reads qa_policy_self_link
   422→   → apps/apps       (workspace: qa)   — reads qa_policy_self_link
   423→
   424→   These can run in parallel since they only depend on sec/waf state output.
   425→
   426→Step 3 (future — staging/prod rollout):
   427→   → apps/gke        (workspace: staging/prod)
   428→   → apps/frontends  (workspace: staging/prod)
   429→   → etc.
   430→```
   431→
   432→## Integration Points
   433→
   434→### IAM Requirements
   435→
   436→The Terraform service account running `sec/waf` currently has permissions in `security-454414`. To deploy policies to other projects, it needs:
   437→
   438→| Permission | Required For |
   439→|------------|-------------|
   440→| `compute.securityPolicies.create` | Creating policies in qa/prod/sha/bi projects |
   441→| `compute.securityPolicies.update` | Updating rules |
   442→| `compute.securityPolicies.delete` | Cleanup |
   443→| `compute.securityPolicies.use` | Required for backend service attachment (granted to LB project SA) |
   444→
   445→The Terraform SA in `sec` must be granted `roles/compute.securityAdmin` in each target project, OR the per-project Terraform SAs must be used via provider credential overrides.
   446→
   447→**Recommended:** Grant `roles/compute.securityAdmin` to the `sec` workspace Terraform SA in each target project:
   448→- `qa-apps-454414`
   449→- `prod-apps-454414`
   450→- `shared-016`
   451→- `liftit-bi`
   452→
   453→### WAF Module Interface Contract
   454→
   455→The private `tf-modules//waf` module must output `policy_self_link` (or `policy_name`) for consumption by `sec/waf/outputs.tf`. Based on the current output in `sec/waf/outputs.tf`:
   456→
   457→```hcl
   458→output "waf_policy_name" {
   459→  value = module.cloud_armor.policy_name
   460→}
   461→```
   462→
   463→The module exposes `policy_name`. For `cloud_armor_policy` in the load balancer module, verify whether it accepts a short name (if policy is in the same project) or requires the full self_link.
   464→
   465→**Since policies will be in the same project as the LBs (not cross-project), the short policy name is sufficient.** The load balancer module's `cloud_armor_policy` parameter is passed to `google_compute_backend_service.security_policy`, which accepts either the name or self_link when the resource is in the same project.
   466→
   467→Update `sec/waf/outputs.tf` to export the policy name per project:
   468→
   469→```hcl
   470→output "qa_policy_name" {
   471→  value       = module.waf_qa.policy_name
   472→  description = "Cloud Armor policy name for qa-apps-454414"
   473→}
   474→
   475→output "prod_policy_name" {
   476→  value       = module.waf_prod.policy_name
   477→  description = "Cloud Armor policy name for prod-apps-454414"
   478→}
   479→
   480→output "staging_policy_name" {
   481→  value       = module.waf_staging.policy_name
   482→  description = "Cloud Armor policy name for stg-apps-454414"
   483→}
   484→
   485→output "sha_policy_name" {
   486→  value       = module.waf_sha.policy_name
   487→  description = "Cloud Armor policy name for shared-016"
   488→}
   489→
   490→output "bi_policy_name" {
   491→  value       = module.waf_bi.policy_name
   492→  description = "Cloud Armor policy name for liftit-bi"
   493→}
   494→```
   495→
   496→### Per-Environment Exclusion Strategy
   497→
   498→Exclusions address false positives for high-risk services. Use CEL expressions in the rule `expr` field combined with host header matching, rather than `preconfigured_waf_config` exclusion blocks, because the existing `tf-modules//waf` rule schema uses `expr` strings. Adding `preconfigured_waf_config` blocks would require changes to the private module interface.
   499→
   500→Preferred CEL-based exclusion pattern (no module changes needed):
   501→
   502→```hcl
   503→# Rule 1030 — SQLi with Superset/Metabase exclusion (BI policy only)
   504→"1030" = {
   505→  action      = "deny(403)"
   506→  description = "SQLi - excluye superset y metabase (BI)"
   507→  preview     = true
   508→  expr        = "evaluatePreconfiguredExpr('sqli-v33-stable') && !request.headers['host'].matches('(?i:superset|metabase)')"
   509→}
   510→```
   511→
   512→For path-based exclusions (Excel loader file uploads, Django admin CSRF):
   513→
   514→```hcl
   515→# Rule 1080 — Method enforcement with Django admin exclusion
   516→"1080" = {
   517→  action      = "deny(403)"
   518→  description = "Method enforcement - excluye Django admin"
   519→  preview     = true
   520→  expr        = "evaluatePreconfiguredExpr('methodenforcement-v33-stable') && !request.path.startsWith('/admin/')"
   521→}
   522→```
   523→
   524→## Anti-Patterns
   525→
   526→### Anti-Pattern 1: Attaching sec Project Policy to Other Projects' Backend Services
   527→
   528→**What people do:** Create one `google_compute_security_policy` in `security-454414` and pass its self_link to `cloud_armor_policy` in LBs running in `qa-apps-454414`.
   529→
   530→**Why it's wrong:** GCP rejects this at the API level — `google_compute_backend_service.security_policy` must reference a policy in the same project. Terraform apply will succeed in creating the policy but fail when attaching it to the backend service with a 403 or 404 error.
   531→
   532→**Do this instead:** Use multi-provider in `sec/waf` to deploy identical policies into each target project. Each LB references the policy in its own project.
   533→
   534→### Anti-Pattern 2: Using Terraform Workspace Strategy for WAF Centralization
   535→
   536→**What people do:** Keep the existing per-workspace deploy pattern (`terraform workspace select qa && terraform apply`) and treat it as "centralized" because it's in `sec/waf`.
   537→
   538→**Why it's wrong:** Current pattern requires running `terraform apply` in 5 different workspaces to update all policies. Policies can drift between workspaces. The IP whitelist is currently different per workspace (correct behavior) but rule sets can diverge unintentionally.
   539→
   540→**Do this instead:** Run `sec/waf` in a single fixed workspace (`sec`) using multi-provider aliases. One apply deploys to all projects atomically. Per-environment variation is explicit in `locals.tf` rule sets, not hidden in separate state files.
   541→
   542→### Anti-Pattern 3: Service-Level WAF Exclusion Config in Consumer Modules
   543→
   544→**What people do:** Add WAF-specific logic to `apps/gke/load-balancer.tf` or other consumer modules — e.g., a local for exclusion paths that modifies how the cloud_armor_policy is named or selected.
   545→
   546→**Why it's wrong:** Consumer modules are LB orchestration. WAF rule logic belongs in `sec/waf`. Splitting WAF configuration across modules makes auditing security posture difficult and creates drift risk.
   547→
   548→**Do this instead:** All WAF rule logic (inclusions, exclusions, sensitivity) lives in `sec/waf/locals.tf`. Consumer modules only read the policy name/self_link from remote state and pass it as a parameter.
   549→
   550→### Anti-Pattern 4: Activating Rules Before Endpoint Analysis
   551→
   552→**What people do:** Set `preview = false` on OWASP rules immediately after attaching policy to LBs.
   553→
   554→**Why it's wrong:** Services like Keycloak, Superset, Excel-loader, Django admin, and TMS-API will generate false positives. Activating rules before analysis creates production incidents.
   555→
   556→**Do this instead:** Attach policy in preview mode (`preview = true` on all deny rules, which is the current state). Monitor Cloud Armor request logs in Cloud Logging for 403 events that would have blocked legitimate traffic. Only promote to active after the full endpoint analysis phase.
   557→
   558→## Staging Module Consideration
   559→
   560→The `apps/gke` module runs in `qa`, `staging`, and `prod` workspaces. For the QA-only milestone, `staging` policy attachment should be deferred. Two options:
   561→
   562→**Option A (recommended):** Deploy `waf_staging` module in `sec/waf` now (alongside `waf_qa`), but keep `staging` LBs with `cloud_armor_policy = null` until staging rollout milestone.
   563→
   564→**Option B:** Only deploy `waf_qa` and defer `waf_staging` until the staging milestone. Keeps staging policy out of state entirely.
   565→
   566→Option A is preferred because it validates the multi-provider pattern works for all projects upfront, and deploying a policy in preview mode to staging has zero traffic impact.
   567→
   568→## Sources
   569→

   571→- [Security policy overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/security-policy-overview) — Policy types, per-project scope (HIGH confidence)
   572→- [Quotas and limits](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/quotas) — Per-project quotas confirming project scope (HIGH confidence)
   573→- [Tune preconfigured WAF rules](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/rule-tuning) — Exclusion config via field operators (HIGH confidence)
   574→- [Cloud Armor best practices](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/best-practices) — Centralized policy recommendation, IaC/Terraform guidance (MEDIUM confidence — fetched, partially summarized)
   575→- [Hierarchical security policies](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/hierarchical-policies-using) — Org/folder-level policies as alternative (HIGH confidence — fetched directly)
   576→- Existing codebase: `sec/waf/waf.tf`, `apps/gke/load-balancer.tf`, `bi/apps/remote-state.tf` — current implementation verified (HIGH confidence)
   577→
   578→---
   579→*Architecture research for: Cloud Armor WAF centralization across GCP projects*
   580→*Researched: 2026-02-24*
